summary: The note describes how cross-disciplinary teaching is reshaping modern classrooms, shifting focus from rote learning to integrated, real-world learning. It surveys strategies such as technology integration, project-based learning, collaborative spaces, teacher training, alternative assessment, community partnerships and parent engagement, illustrated with dated examples from various schools and quotes from educators between September 2023 and March 2024.
one_line: Overview of cross-disciplinary teaching strategies in modern classrooms, with school examples and educator quotes from 2023-2024.
key_facts: Cross-disciplinary learning removes walls between subjects so students can connect and apply knowledge, fostering critical thinking, creativity and collaboration.
Johnathan Carter, principal at Green Valley High School, said on October 15, 2023 that students are more engaged when learning is relevant and interconnected.
Alma Stewart, an educational consultant, said on December 1, 2023 that technology intertwined with cross-disciplinary methods lets students explore subjects in depth and from multiple perspectives.
Technology examples for cross-disciplinary learning include virtual labs, simulation software and online repositories of cross-curricular lesson plans.
According to the Buck Institute for Education, project-based learning (PBL) involves long-term, collaborative projects that integrate subject areas and are curriculum-based and real-world oriented.

On November 5, 2023, Green View Elementary launched a school-wide PBL initiative on environmental sustainability, integrating science, social studies, mathematics and language arts; PBL coordinator Maria Gonzalez led the program commentary.

Franklin Middle School redesigned its classrooms in September 2023 with mobile workstations and communal areas; principal Daniel Levinson reported more student participation and peer-to-peer tutoring.

The Jackson District began a professional development series on September 20, 2023 covering collaborative teaching strategies and cross-curricular planning; teacher Evelyn Richards said it transformed her approach.
Portfolios, peer reviews and reflective journals are suggested assessment methods; researcher Linda Hart presented a report on January 10, 2024 calling for multi-faceted assessment.
Eastgate Academy partnered with a local tech startup on February 24, 2024 so students could work on real software projects combining computer science, mathematics and business studies.
Principal Jennifer Smith of Eastgate Academy said community partnerships expose students to real-life applications and mentorship.
Oakwood Secondary held a 'Family Science Night' on March 8, 2024, where parents did experiments with their children; community liaison officer Tom Weber commented on it.
